answer.rationale: Hard constraint is no added delivery risk: the primary contract lapses in 14 days with no auto-renew, the line is at 94% with zero buffer, and only one decision fits this cycle. memory_c1 is the only inherited result that keeps integration and scheduled deliveries intact, so renewing the incumbent is the action that does not raise stockout risk. The 18% spend cut is unmet because the incumbent already refused to reopen price; switching (memory_c2) is the historical cost lever but “quick” onboarding is too underspecified to move primary volume under these constraints—verifying that archive before treating switch as feasible. Deferral (memory_c5) was for non-critical month-to-month service and does not cover a non-auto-renewing production contract. A second source does not replace the expiring primary in a one-action window. Residual risk flagged: finance mandate remains open and any slip in the 14-day renewal close has no operational buffer.
